clue.text: Male musician's first appearance on radio

definitions.text: Male musician's first appearance on radio

parts.words: Male musician's first appearance on radio
parts.note: surface reading: a male singer's debut broadcast

parts.words: Male musician's first appearance on radio
parts.note: setter's reading: the letter for Male, also the musician's first letter, as it is spoken in the radio operators' alphabet

explanation.surface: A singer makes his first ever broadcast on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: M stands for male and begins musician; in the NATO phonetic alphabet used on radio, M is said as MIKE, which is also the microphone a musician sings into.
explanation.definitionFit: The phonetic alphabet code word for the letter M is Mike, and a mike is the microphone any performer stands at.

clue.text: Son of Scots playing on air? That's dandy!

indicators.note: letters that are playing are performing in a different arrangement, so the next words get rearranged

parts.note: Mac is the Gaelic prefix meaning son of, found in Scottish surnames

explanation.surface: A Scottish lad playing music on the radio is praised as splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dandy' looks like the exclamation 'that's dandy!' meaning great, but it is the noun for a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: In the eighteenth century a macaroni was a fashionable young man who affected continental styles, a fop or dandy, as in Yankee Doodle.

clue.text: Male holding very large pipe starts to hum October Song etc

indicators.note: a man holding something has it in his grip, so the next item sits inside him

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

parts.words: starts to hum October Song etc
parts.note: a bonus: the opening letters of these four words spell the same answer again

explanation.surface: A man clutching an enormous pipe begins humming an autumn tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail of the clue is a second, independent route: read the first letters of hum, October, Song and etc. October Song is also a Robbie Williams track.
explanation.definitionFit: A hose is a flexible tube or pipe for carrying water, as in a garden hose.

clue.text: See 12
Flat point between fringes of Smoke Shovelling suit

indicators.note: the item sits between the outer letters, the edges of the next word

parts.note: the first and last letters of Smoke
a pad is a flat, a place to live
S for south, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone shovels smoke out of a flat, a strange chore.
explanation.walkthrough: PAD goes between the edges of Smoke, then the compass point is added at the end; the setter reads Flat point slightly out of order. A pad is slang for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades are tools for shovelling earth and also one of the four card suits, so the plural fits both senses.

clue.text: King Charles not to be taken outside? Preposterous!

indicators.note: the phrase that goes outside wraps around the royal abbreviation

parts.note: something inedible must not be eaten
Carolus Rex, the Latin royal cipher of King Charles

explanation.surface: An outraged King Charles is told he may not go out, which he finds absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken outside' sounds like being escorted out, but 'not to be taken' is food you cannot eat and 'outside' is the wrapping instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something preposterous is too absurd to believe, which is what incredible literally means.

clue.text: Drum one doctor found in short story

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the word loses its last letter
what is found in something sits inside it

parts.note: a tale without its last letter
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor appears in a brief tale about a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbal, or timbale, is a kettledrum, the old name for the instrument now called the timpani.

clue.text: Opposed to a mother's ruin

parts.note: mother's ruin is an old British nickname for gin

explanation.surface: Someone is against their mother's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother's ruin reads as a family disaster, but it is the Victorian slang name for gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of against, used to mean opposed to something.

clue.text: Honest villain seen circling minute 6-foot stage?

indicators.note: the villain circling something goes around it, holding it inside

explanation.surface: A trusted rogue moves around a tiny six-foot platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like tiny, and '6-foot stage' like a small platform, but it is the life stage of a six-legged insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final adult stage of an insect, and insects have six legs, hence six feet.

clue.text: Mischief-maker close at hand

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is standing nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impending is about to happen, imminent or near at hand in time.

clue.text: Given glossy coat, tailless llama needed to be replaced

indicators.note: without a tail, each of the two words loses its final letter
letters to be replaced are put back in new positions

explanation.surface: A llama has lost its tail and must be swapped for a shinier one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needed' looks like a link word, but it is fodder too: tailless trims both llama and needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamelled things have been covered with enamel, a hard shiny coating or glaze.

clue.text: Singers that tweet about Prince as former actor

indicators.note: the singers go about, around, the royal name

parts.note: Prince William, the Duke of Cambridge

explanation.surface: Pop singers post on Twitter about a royal who was once an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singers that tweet' suggests musicians on Twitter; they are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The American comedian and film star died in 2014, so he is a former actor, famed for Mrs Doubtfire and Good Morning, Vietnam.

clue.text: Some guts shown by couple meeting a bad end earlier

indicators.note: a bad version of the word is a corrupted one, its letters disordered
earlier moves the scrambled word ahead of the single letter it follows in the clue

explanation.surface: A pair come to a nasty end, with their entrails on display.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'a bad end', but the scrambled word comes first and the a last.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine; its plural names more than one of these sections of gut.

clue.text: Ornamentation of French horn by Debussy?

parts.note: cor is French for horn, as the French composer would say it

explanation.surface: A query about the decorative flourishes in a French horn part written by Debussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' reads as the instrument, but French belongs with 'of', and Debussy signals a second French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the decoration and furnishing of a room, its ornamental scheme.

clue.text: Like 12, passed as fair

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to the actor suggests someone judged fair, like him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like 12' tempts you to think of the actor at 12; it refers to the number twelve itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An even-handed judgement treats everyone equally and impartially, which is what fair means.

clue.text: Sold out through saying: "If it can go wrong, it will"

definitions.text: "If it can go wrong, it will"

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the word preceding it is scrambled
running through something places it inside

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A shop sold out, proving the old adage that whatever can go wrong will.
explanation.definitionFit: Sod's law is the British name for the principle that anything that can go wrong will, also called Murphy's law.

clue.text: Female from Western state

explanation.surface: A girl comes from a state out West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western state' looks like Oregon or Nevada, but the state is in Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Female as a noun is a woman, an adult human of that sex.

clue.text: Indian chief, 100, with very bad back

parts.note: the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: going back means reading the word from its end

explanation.surface: A hundred-year-old chief of a tribe has a terrible back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian chief' suggests a Native American leader; it is Robert Clive, who led the British in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Clive, Clive of India, was the eighteenth-century commander and governor who headed British power in Bengal.

clue.text: Number not good for offspring

indicators.note: not here means without, so the following letter is dropped

parts.note: a number is a piece of music in a show

explanation.surface: A child is judged to be no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' wants to mean a numeral; it is a musical number.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, one of a parent's offspring.

clue.text: Submarines torpedoed? U-boat's heading away — close call!

indicators.note: torpedoed things are blown apart and scattered
away means these letters are taken out

parts.note: U plus the first letter of boat

explanation.surface: Submarines fire torpedoes but a U-boat turns aside just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: U and B are removed from the subs before the remaining letters are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an incident where disaster was only narrowly avoided, the same as a close call.

clue.text: Slovenly Scotswoman needed to get cleaner? "Maybe Someday" covers that
Delays before second cashier takes dodgy bet

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the word is twisted
everything assembled is placed ahead of the final letter
the cashier takes something in, holding it inside

parts.note: to cashier is to dismiss, to sack

explanation.surface: A bank clerk places a suspicious wager, holding things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a bank clerk but is the verb meaning to dismiss from service.
explanation.definitionFit: Setbacks are reverses or hold-ups that slow progress, so they work as delays.

clue.text: His opera briefly involved fruit

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A composer's short opera involved some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosehip is the red fruit of the rose plant, used for syrup and tea.

clue.text: Musician's essential for group of Arabs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a violinist or guitarist cannot play without one
second meaning: the horses kept in one racing stable

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabs' suggests people, but Arabs are also a breed of horse, and a stable's horses are its string.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument needs strings to sound, and a racing trainer's set of horses is called a string.

clue.text: Rock group circuit's rising golfer

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track

explanation.surface: A rock band's tour circuit is gaining popularity with a sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Carl Palmer of the rock group Emerson, Lake and Palmer is a red herring; the definition is the golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Palmer was the celebrated American golfer, winner of seven major championships.

clue.text: Two articles about underwear in sacred text

definitions.note: adjectival phrase: Avestan describes something in the language of the Avesta

indicators.note: the two words go about, around, the garment

parts.note: the indefinite articles a and an
in Britain a vest is an undershirt

explanation.surface: A couple of pieces of writing about underwear appear in a holy book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests items of clothing or writing; here they are grammar words. A British vest is worn under a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Avestan is the ancient Iranian language of the Avesta, the scriptures of Zoroastrianism, so it means written in that holy book.

clue.text: Flying fish eater, one whose lover regularly swam north

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont each night to his beloved Hero

explanation.surface: A fish predator in flight, and a mythical swimmer heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying fish' looks like the gliding sea creature, but it is a bird that flies and eats fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird that spears fish, and it flies, so it is a flying fish eater.

clue.text: Messy mix in middle of The Tree

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter only

explanation.surface: A jumble sits right in the middle of the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A hash is a jumbled mess or muddle, as in making a hash of things.

clue.text: Light colour for soot?

explanation.surface: A question about whether a pale shade could be the colour of soot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light colour' reads as a pale shade; it is a light followed by a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampblack is the fine black carbon soot deposited by burning oil lamps, used as a pigment.

clue.text: Musician ultimately in wrong group

indicators.note: the letter goes in, inside, the next word
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A musician ends up in the wrong group.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of people, especially a group of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Caring daughter supports relatives

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting item stands underneath the other one

explanation.surface: A loving daughter looks after her family.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind person is considerate and caring towards others.

clue.text: Feel inferior? That's stupid

parts.note: less means lower in status, inferior

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop feeling inferior because it is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feel inferior' reads as one idea, low self-esteem, but splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something senseless lacks sense or reason, so it is foolish and stupid.

clue.text: One taking snap of beatnik only

indicators.note: of here means made from, taken out of the letters that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone photographs only the beatnik.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikon is a well-known Japanese brand of camera, a device that takes snaps or photographs.
